title: Trace comparison for a finite flat morphism of smooth curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme equipped with a smooth morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ of relative dimension one, and let $f:X\to\mathbf P^1_k$ be a morphism over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ that is finite and flat. Here $\mathbf P^1_k$ is the standard projective line of [def-sc-p1-standard]. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ (respectively $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $\mathbf P^1_k$), write $\Omega^1_{A/k}$ (respectively $\Omega^1_{R/k}$) for the $A$-module (respectively $R$-module) generated by symbols $da$ (respectively $dr$), subject to $d(a+a')=da+da'$, $d(aa')=a\,da'+a'\,da$, and $dk=0$; these modules glue to the relative Kähler differential sheaves $\Omega^1_{X/k}$ and $\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}$. Then there exists an $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-linear morphism $\tau:f_*\Omega^1_{X/k}\to\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}$ such that the $f_*\mathcal O_X$-linear comparison map $$f_*\Omega^1_{X/k}\longrightarrow\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}}(f_*\mathcal O_X,\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}),\qquad \omega\longmapsto\bigl(a\longmapsto\tau(a\omega)\bigr)$$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: A finite f is proper. Its composite with the proper projective-line structure map is the structure map of X, by the over-k hypothesis. Thus X is proper, and both X and the projective line are Noetherian. Choose standard derived localizations and the restriction R of Rf_* and its right adjoint a via [lem-pc-noetherian-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint]. The comparison of R with Rf_* is the identity inclusion comparison.

Apply [lem-sc-smooth-curve-upper-shriek-differentials] to obtain a representative K of Omega_Y[0] and an isomorphism a(K) to Omega_X[0]. The projective line is smooth of relative dimension one and Omega_Y is invertible. Apply [lem-sc-finite-flat-duality-evaluation] to obtain M, its degree-zero identification e0 with a(K), an isomorphism e:f_*M to Hom(f_*O_X,Omega_Y), and an evaluation map epsilon satisfying epsilon(m)=e(m)(1) and e(m)(b)=epsilon(bm). Full faithfulness of the single-complex functor takes e0 followed by the differential identification to a sheaf isomorphism d:M to Omega_X.

Define tau=f_*(d inverse) followed by epsilon. Compose f_*Hom(O_X,Omega_X) to f_*Omega_X (evaluation at 1), then f_*d inverse, then e, giving an isomorphism b. To check that b is the library comparison map, work on every open U and smaller open W. A section phi of Hom(O_X,Omega_X) satisfies phi_W(x)=x phi_W(1). Naturality of phi and d inverse identifies d inverse(phi_W(1)) with the restriction of d inverse(phi_U(1)). Naturality of e identifies its evaluations over W with the restriction of e over U. The two evaluation identities of the finite-duality theorem then give tau_W(phi_W(x))=e_W(x d inverse(phi_W(1)))(1)=e_W(d inverse(phi_W(1)))(x)=b_U(phi)_W(x). Extensionality proves the comparison equals b.hom, so it is an isomorphism.
